text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Lagos state government doles out 8.5 million naira for the treatment in Israel of Nigerian goal keeper Joseph Dosu, who was severely injured in a car crash two weeks ago.
- Swiss court acquits Nigerian human rights activist Clement Nwankwo of theft charge.
- Fuel road tanker drivers urge federal government to tackle current petrol shortage urgently.
- Nigerian information minister Walter Ofonagoro suggests that the Dakar-based Pan African News Agency should be privatised to relieve it of its present financial problems.
- Oil minister Dan Etete lashes out at critics of his ministry over the current fuel shortage including financial minister Anthony Ani and Lagos state military administrator Colonel Mohammed Marwa.
- Opposition NADECO group and others blame government for fuel crunch.
- Embassies of United States and Britain deny government charges that Nigerians who apply for visas to their countries are maltreated.
